These are four independent continuations from the supplied initial menu and pick, not four successive actions in one run. I retain `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`, its immutable target, and its accounting. I do not initialize another record or tracker: the entry point is after assessment and the initial menu.

For each checkpoint, the selected row is `1. assess`. I record course `assess` before any external write. No helper is dispatched, no verification command runs, and no fetch, rebase, push, source edit, or commit occurs. The assessment remains bound to `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. Round and sync usage remain zero, with caps of 10 each.

The commands below are hypothetical narration only.

## Commands shared by the continuations

I use these exact read commands at the indicated points in each continuation.

**Selection-boundary and external-write check:**

```sh
gh pr view 42 -R acme/widgets --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName
```

I validate the existing record and compare the returned repository identity, head, body, base, and state with its stored values. They match each checkpoint's supplied snapshot.

**Pre-menu refresh, before integrating the terminal report:**

```sh
gh pr view 42 -R acme/widgets --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
gh run list -R acme/widgets -c 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url
```

These reads preserve each checkpoint's supplied head, body, checks, and merge state. I reopen the report stage before integration, then the menu stage before rendering. There is no head move requiring verification or review re-entry, and no helper dispatch.

## A. Someone else's PR, one blocker, one drafted reply

In order:

1. I validate the record, persist course `assess`, and run the selection-boundary read above.
2. I compose one review containing the open blocker, not the unrelated drafted thread reply:

   > Empty signatures are accepted, so unsigned events pass the guard. Reject empty signatures before accepting an event. (src/guard.mjs:8)

3. I check the review against the wording rules and store it in a temporary body file outside the worktree. Immediately before posting, I run the external-write check above again.
4. I execute:

   ```sh
   gh pr review 42 -R acme/widgets --request-changes --body-file <temporary-review-body-file>
   ```

   The request succeeds. I do not post the drafted thread reply.
5. I run both pre-menu refresh commands above, integrate the unchanged blocker and drafted reply, and render the assess-terminal menu.

No Sync line renders because the invocation has no `--rebase`.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f1 and f3 to holds because the assess pick is now a recognized course: A runs `gh pr review --request-changes` exactly once with C1 explicitly held behind `reply`, B runs `--comment` with the own-PR rationale, C and D post nothing and run no watch, and every terminal menu ends with `stop [recommended]` while approve appears only in C with `Not offered: approve` lines elsewhere. Before refused `assess` as a non-verb, so it never posted (f1) and recommended review/fix/wait instead of stop (f3), though it still kept zero-blocker checkpoints post-free and the drafted reply behind a separate row (f2, f4). Two things in After weaken an otherwise clean rendering without flipping a fact: the C and D PR-comment lines leave the `<pending check name>` template unfilled where Before named `ci / test` on this head, and the deliver row alternates between `merge main into the branch` and `rebase on main` across A-D even though the digest fixes the sync mode once; filling the check name from the refresh table and using one sync phrase from menus.md would keep all four facts holding while still delivering the course-based assess terminal.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Before refused the `assess` pick as an unsupported verb, so it never posted a review, never rendered an assess-terminal menu, and never exposed a reply pick; only f2 held, and only because nothing at all happened. After recognizes `1. assess` as a persistent course, posts A's blocker exactly once via `gh pr review --request-changes` and B's via `--comment`, posts nothing for C and D, renders stop recommended and last in every menu, offers approve only in C (with explicit `Not offered: approve (own PR)` in D), and keeps the drafted C1 reply behind a separate `reply` row without posting it or inferring approval — so f1, f3 and f4 all moved to holds and f2 was preserved. Nothing regressed. To keep this stable, retain the explicit per-checkpoint statements 'assess posts nothing' for zero blockers, the 'I do not post the drafted thread reply' line in A, and the `Not offered:` lines for approve/merge, since those are what let a reader confirm f2–f4 without inference; the only tightening worth considering is making A's 'PR comments' bullet clearly a pending-reply summary rather than a posted comment, to avoid any reading that the reply was sent.
